topics.title: Column file metadata and spec simplifications
topics.summary: Gábor is updating the column file metadata pull request based on the v4 spec. The changes to simplify the spec are removing format_version and using only two snapshot IDs, created and modified. The TrackingBuilder will set data_sequence_number to null for column file updates, so that the library inherits a new sequence number when manifests are written.

topics.title: Read-side stitching architecture
topics.summary: The notes say the DataFileReadBuilder is approved for data files only, while delete files go directly to the FormatModelRegistry. A StitcherRegistry will manage stitcher implementations, which depend on the internal row representation such as Spark InternalRow, and a StitchLayout map gives field access in stitched rows without moving data. The RowAlignedStitchingIterable aligns readers by advancing them to a common row position, covering initial split offsets and row groups skipped by predicate filtering; the SkippingCloseableIterable that provides advanceToPosition is Parquet-only for now.
decisions: The DataFileReadBuilder is used for data files only; delete files go directly to the FormatModelRegistry (AI-generated notes).

topics.title: Commit API strategy
topics.summary: Steven proposed two options for the v4 commit API: a dedicated table.newUpdateColumns() interface, or a generic table.newUpdateFiles() interface that handles column updates first and expands to other operations later. The decision was to proceed with a simple update and append interface first. The reason given is to learn about API concerns for column-only changes, with no row adds or deletes, before integrating into a more complex unified v4 writer.
decisions: Proceed with a simple update and append commit interface first (AI-generated notes).
